speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; have you noticed any abdominal distension or blood in your stools?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with Midgut Volvulus. The patient is a term newborn with bilious vomiting and feeding intolerance. A family history of pyloric stenosis is noted, but the presence of bilious vomiting in a neonate is a surgical emergency until volvulus is ruled out; immediate evaluation for malrotation is required.
